testCases.label: Add VirtualMachines agent pool via az CLI preview with multiple SKUs
testCases.notes: az aks nodepool add --vm-set-type VirtualMachines --vm-sizes Standard_D4s_v3,Standard_D8s_v3 exited 1 with preview CLI/client validation "We only accept single sku size for scale profile"; iteration65 source inspection found the active aks-preview decorator enforces len(--vm-sizes)==1 before constructing manual/autoscale scale profiles.

diagnosis.summary: The add help example advertises comma-separated multi-SKU input, but active aks-preview source rejects multi-value --vm-sizes for VirtualMachines scale profiles.

testCases.label: Enable and update autoscaler settings for a VirtualMachines agent pool via az CLI preview
testCases.notes: Starting from a single-SKU manual VirtualMachines pool, az aks nodepool update --enable-cluster-autoscaler persisted virtualMachinesProfile.scale.autoscale[0] with Standard_D4s_v4 min/max; az aks nodepool update --update-cluster-autoscaler --node-vm-size Standard_D4s_v6 persisted a single autoscale profile with the new size and min/max.

testCases.label: Add and delete an additional single-SKU manual scale profile on a VirtualMachines agent pool via az CLI preview
testCases.notes: Starting from a one-profile manual VirtualMachines pool, az aks nodepool manual-scale add --vm-sizes Standard_D4s_v6 --node-count 1 exited 0 and persisted two manual profiles (Standard_D4s_v4 and Standard_D4s_v6); manual-scale delete of the second profile exited 0 and returned to one profile. Enabling autoscaler while two manual profiles existed failed client-side by design. manual-scale update --current-vm-sizes Standard_D4s_v6 --node-count 2 unexpectedly failed with "None is invalid" because the CLI validates omitted --vm-sizes as an empty list; this does not negate add/delete multiple-profile support.

On staging cluster approuting67, az aks approuting enable exited 0 and show returned webAppRouting.enabled=true; az aks approuting disable --yes then exited 0 and follow-up show returned ingressProfile.webAppRouting.enabled=false with identity fields null.

On staging cluster approuting68, az aks approuting enable --enable-default-domain exited 0; follow-up az aks show and az aks approuting defaultdomain show returned defaultDomain.enabled=true with autogenerated domainName 6a0c015aae6c7800012e441e.eastus2.aksapp.io.

diagnosis.summary: The active aks-preview help example advertises two comma-separated --vm-sizes, but agentpool_decorator.py rejects any VirtualMachines scale profile with len(sizes) != 1 before constructing either manual or autoscale payload. Staging autoscale update supports one autoscale profile with one size, not multi-SKU.

judgments.nextAction: For add/update VirtualMachines pool paths, use one supported SKU per manual/autoscale profile. Treat the comma-separated multi-SKU add help example as misleading unless a separate manual-scale subcommand or REST path is intentionally validated.

judgments.summary: The documented VirtualMachines autoscaler update path is supported for one autoscale profile with one VM size: enable autoscaler converted manual Standard_D4s_v4 to autoscale, and update-cluster-autoscaler changed that profile to Standard_D4s_v6 with min/max persisted.

diagnosis.summary: Swagger says only one AutoScaleProfile is allowed and CLI source requires one --vm-sizes value when building VirtualMachines scale profiles; this is not multi-SKU support.

judgments.summary: The separate preview manual-scale subcommands are the supported CLI path for multiple manual VirtualMachines scale profiles: add persisted a second single-SKU manual profile and delete removed it in eastus2 staging.

diagnosis.summary: Multi-profile manual scaling is supported as multiple single-size ManualScaleProfile entries managed by az aks nodepool manual-scale add/delete, not as a comma-separated multi-SKU --vm-sizes value on nodepool add. Each manual-scale command still accepts exactly one size.

judgments.nextAction: Use manual-scale add/delete for multiple manual profiles; avoid count-only manual-scale update until the CLI validation bug for omitted --vm-sizes is fixed or intentionally model that bug separately.

judgments.summary: Staging public CLI App Routing disablement is accepted by RP: after successful enablement, az aks approuting disable --yes exited 0 and persisted ingressProfile.webAppRouting.enabled=false with App Routing identity removed/null.

Staging public CLI App Routing default-domain enablement is accepted by RP: az aks approuting enable --enable-default-domain exited 0 and persisted webAppRouting.enabled=true plus defaultDomain.enabled=true with an autogenerated aksapp.io domain name.
